For what we believe by Thy revelation of Thy glory, the same do we believe of Thy Son, the same of the Holy Ghost, without difference or separation. So that in confessing the true and everlasting Godhead, distinction in persons, unity in essence, and equality in majesty may be adored. L.kuo: In the beginning was the Word, and the Word was with God, and the Word was God. The same was in the beginning with God. All things were made by Him, and without Him was made nothing that was made: in Him was life, and the life was the Light of men; and the Light shineth in darkness, and the darkness did not comprehend it. There was a man sent from God, whose name was John. This man came for a witness, to testify concerning the Light, that all might believe through Him. He was not the Light, but he was to testify concerning the Light. That was the true Light, which enlighteneth every man that cometh into this world. He was in the world, and the world was made by Him, and the world knew Him not. He came unto His own, and His own received Him not. But as many as received Him to them He gave power to become sons of God, to them that believe in His Name, who are born not of blood, nor of the will of the flesh, nor of the will of man, but of God. ^Here all kneel.^ And the Word was made flesh, and dwelt among us: and we saw His glory, the glory as of the Only begotten of the Father, full of grace and truth.

L.aar: In illo témpore: Dixit Iesus discípulis suis parábolam hanc: Homo péregre proficíscens vocávit servos suos, et trádidit illis bona sua. Et uni dedit quinque talénta, álii autem duo, álii vero unum, unicuíque secúndum própriam virtútem, et proféctus est statim. Abiit autem, qui quinque talénta accéperat, et operátus est in eis, et lucrátus est ália quinque. Simíliter et, qui duo accéperat, lucrátus est ália duo. Qui autem unum accéperat, ábiens fodit in terram, et abscóndit pecúniam dómini sui. Post multum vero témporis venit dóminus servórum illórum, et pósuit ratiónem cum eis. Et accédens qui quinque talénta accéperat, óbtulit ália quinque talénta, dicens: Dómine, quinque talénta tradidísti mihi, ecce, ália quinque superlucrátus sum. Ait illi dóminus eius: Euge, serve bone et fidélis, quia super pauca fuísti fidélis, super multa te constítuam: intra in gáudium dómini tui. Accéssit autem et qui duo talénta accéperat, et ait: Dómine, duo talénta tradidísti mihi, ecce, ália duo lucrátus sum. Ait illi dóminus eius: Euge, serve bone et fidélis, quia super pauca fuísti fidélis, super multa te constítuam: intra in gáudium dómini tui.
L.in0: At that time, Jesus spoke this parable to His disciples: A man going abroad, called his servants and handed over his goods to them. And to one he gave five talents, to another two, and to another one, to each according to his particular ability, and then he went on his journey. And he who had received the five talents went and traded with them, and gained five more. In like manner, he who had received the two gained two more. But he who had received the one went away and dug in the earth and hid his master’s money. Then after a long time the master of those servants came and settled accounts with them. And he who had received the five talents came and brought five other talents, saying, ‘Master, you handed over to me five talents; behold, I have gained five others in addition.’ His master said to him, ‘Well done, good and faithful servant; because you have been faithful over a few things, I will set you over many; enter into the joy of your master.’ And he also who had received the two talents came, and said, ‘Master, you handed over to me two talents; behold, I have gained two more.’ His master said to him, ‘Well done, good and faithful servant; because you have been faithful over a few things, I will set you over many; enter into the joy of your master.’

Ideo iureiurándo fecit illum Dóminus créscere in plebem suam. Benedictiónem ómnium géntium dedit illi, et testaméntum suum confirmávit super caput eius. Agnóvit eum in benedictiónibus suis: conservávit illi misericórdiam suam: et invénit grátiam coram óculis Dómini. Magnificávit eum in conspéctu regum: et dedit illi corónam glóriæ. Státuit illi testaméntum ætérnum, et dedit illi sacerdótium magnum: et beatificávit illum in glória. Fungi sacerdótio, et habére laudem in nómine ipsíus, et offérre illi incénsum dignum in odórem suavitátis.
L.itr: Behold, a great priest, who in his days pleased God, and was found just; and in the time of wrath he was made a reconciliation. There was not found the like to him, who kept the law of the Most High. Therefore, by an oath, the Lord made him to increase among his people. He gave him the blessing of all nations, and confirmed His covenant upon his head. He acknowledged him in His blessings; He preserved for him His mercy; and he found grace before the eyes of the Lord. He glorified him in the sight of kings, and gave him a crown of glory. He made an everlasting covenant with him, and gave him a great priesthood; and made him blessed in glory. To execute the office of the priesthood, and to have praise in His name, and to offer Him a worthy incense for an odor of sweetness.

L.spt: ^79:13^ Ut quid destruxísti macériam eius: * et vindémiant eam omnes, qui prætergrediúntur viam?
L.spv: ^79:14^ Exterminávit eam aper de silva: * et singuláris ferus depástus est eam.
L.spx: ^79:15^ Deus virtútum, convértere: * réspice de cælo, et vide, et vísita víneam istam.
L.sq0: ^79:16^ Et pérfice eam, quam plantávit déxtera tua: * et super fílium hóminis, quem confirmásti tibi.
L.sq1: ^79:17^ Incénsa igni, et suffóssa * ab increpatióne vultus tui períbunt.
L.sq3: ^79:18^ Fiat manus tua super virum déxteræ tuæ: * et super fílium hóminis, quem confirmásti tibi.
L.sq6: ^79:19^ Et non discédimus a te, vivificábis nos: * et nomen tuum invocábimus.
L.sq7: ^79:20^ Dómine, Deus virtútum, convérte nos: * et osténde fáciem tuam, et salvi érimus.
L.sq9: ^79:9^ Thou hast brought a vineyard out of Egypt: * thou hast cast out the Gentiles and planted it.
L.spo: ^79:10^ Thou wast the guide of its journey in its sight: * thou plantedst the roots thereof, and it filled the land.
L.spq: ^79:11^ The shadow of it covered the hills: * and the branches thereof the cedars of God.
L.sps: ^79:12^ It stretched forth its branches unto the sea, * and its boughs unto the river.
L.spu: ^79:13^ Why hast thou broken down the hedge thereof, * so that all they who pass by the way do pluck it?
L.spw: ^79:14^ The boar out of the wood hath laid it waste: * and a singular wild beast hath devoured it.
L.spy: ^79:15^ Turn again, O God of hosts, * look down from heaven, and see, and visit this vineyard:
L.spz: ^79:16^ And perfect the same which thy right hand hath planted: * and upon the son of man whom thou hast confirmed for thyself.
L.sq2: ^79:17^ Things set on fire and dug down * shall perish at the rebuke of thy countenance.
L.sq4: ^79:18^ Let thy hand be upon the man of thy right hand: * and upon the son of man whom thou hast confirmed for thyself.
L.sq5: ^79:19^ And we depart not from thee, thou shalt quicken us: * and we will call upon thy name.
L.sq8: ^79:20^ O Lord God of hosts, convert us: * and shew thy face, and we shall be saved.
L.x0g: ^Ant.^ Éxcita, Dómine, poténtiam tuam, ut salvos fácias nos.
L.w8e: ^Ant.^ Stir up thy might, O Lord, and come to save us.
L.tyw: ^Ant.^ Beáti, qui hábitant * in domo tua, Dómine.
L.tzs: ^Ant.^ Blessed are they * that dwell in thy house, O Lord.
L.tyx: ^Ant.^ Beáti, qui hábitant in domo tua, Dómine.
L.tzu: ^Ant.^ Blessed are they that dwell in thy house, O Lord.
L.vf2: ^Ant.^ Misericórdia et véritas * præcédent fáciem tuam, Dómine.
L.veq: ^Ant.^ Mercy and truth * shall go before thy face, O Lord.
L.vf3: ^Ant.^ Misericórdia et véritas præcédent fáciem tuam, Dómine.
L.ver: ^Ant.^ Mercy and truth shall go before thy face, O Lord.
L.ucv: ^Ant.^ Dómine, * probásti me et cognovísti me. ^‡^
L.pfa: ^138:1^ Dómine, probásti me, et cognovísti me: * ^‡^ tu cognovísti sessiónem meam, et resurrectiónem meam.
L.udd: ^Ant.^ Dómine, probásti me et cognovísti me.
L.vao: ^Ant.^ Lord, * thou hast proved me, and known me. ^‡^
L.pfb: ^138:1^ Lord, thou hast proved me, and known me: * ^‡^ thou hast known my sitting down, and my rising up.
L.vbb: ^Ant.^ Lord, thou hast proved me, and known me.
L.vev: ^Ant.^ Mirabília ópera tua, * Dómine, et ánima mea cognóscit nimis.
L.vew: ^Ant.^ Mirabília ópera tua, Dómine, et ánima mea cognóscit nimis.
L.wza: ^Ant.^ Wonderful are thy works * and my soul knoweth right well.
L.wzb: ^Ant.^ Wonderful are thy works and my soul knoweth right well.
L.vhu: ^Ant.^ Ne derelínquas me, * Dómine, virtus salútis meæ.
L.vhv: ^Ant.^ Ne derelínquas me, Dómine, virtus salútis meæ.
L.ubn: ^Ant.^ Do not thou forsake me, * O Lord, the strength of my salvation.
L.ubo: ^Ant.^ Do not thou forsake me, O Lord, the strength of my salvation.
L.ucq: ^Ant.^ Dómine, * clamávi ad te, exáudi me. ^‡^
L.pk4: ^140:1^ Dómine, clamávi ad te, exáudi me: * ^‡^ inténde voci meæ, cum clamávero ad te.
L.ud6: ^Ant.^ Dómine, clamávi ad te, exáudi me.
L.uws: ^Ant.^ I have cried to thee, * O Lord, hear me. ^‡^
L.pk5: ^140:1^ I have cried to thee, O Lord, hear me: * ^‡^ hearken to my voice, when I cry to thee.
L.uwt: ^Ant.^ I have cried to thee, O Lord, hear me.
L.ug7: ^Ant.^ Educ de custódia * ánimam meam, Dómine, ad confiténdum nómini tuo.
L.ug8: ^Ant.^ Educ de custódia ánimam meam, Dómine, ad confiténdum nómini tuo.
L.u0m: ^Ant.^ Bring my soul * out of prison, O Lord, that I may praise thy name.
L.u0n: ^Ant.^ Bring my soul out of prison, O Lord, that I may praise thy name.
L.wui: ^Ant.^ Voce mea * ad Dóminum clamávi: neque obliviscétur miseréri Deus.
L.uwo: ^Ant.^ I have cried * to the Lord with my voice, do not forget to show mercy, O God.
L.7ru: ^76:14^ Deus, in sancto via tua: quis Deus magnus sicut Deus noster? * tu es Deus qui facis mirabília.
L.7rw: ^76:15^ Notam fecísti in pópulis virtútem tuam: * redemísti in brácchio tuo pópulum tuum, fílios Iacob et Ioseph.
L.7rz: ^76:17^ Vidérunt te aquæ, Deus, vidérunt te aquæ: * et timuérunt, et turbátæ sunt abýssi.
L.7s2: ^76:18^ Multitúdo sónitus aquárum: * vocem dedérunt nubes.
L.7s3: ^76:18^ Étenim sagíttæ tuæ tránseunt: * vox tonítrui tui in rota.
L.7s4: ^76:19^ Illuxérunt coruscatiónes tuæ orbi terræ: * commóta est, et contrémuit terra.
L.7s6: ^76:20^ In mari via tua, et sémitæ tuæ in aquis multis: * et vestígia tua non cognoscéntur.
L.7s8: ^76:21^ Deduxísti sicut oves pópulum tuum, * in manu Móysi et Aaron.
L.7rv: ^76:14^ Thy way, O God, is in the holy place: who is the great God like our God? * Thou art the God that dost wonders.
L.7rx: ^76:15^ Thou hast made thy power known among the nations: * with thy arm thou hast redeemed thy people, the children of Jacob and of Joseph.
L.7ry: ^76:17^ The waters saw thee, O God, the waters saw thee: * and they were afraid, and the depths were troubled.
L.7s1: ^76:18^ Great was the noise of the waters: * the clouds sent out a sound.
L.7s0: ^76:18^ For thy arrows pass: * the voice of thy thunder in a wheel.
L.7s5: ^76:19^ Thy lightnings enlightened the world: * the earth shook and trembled.
L.7s7: ^76:20^ Thy way is in the sea, and thy paths in many waters: * and thy footsteps shall not be known.
L.7s9: ^76:21^ Thou hast conducted thy people like sheep, * by the hand of Moses and Aaron.
L.wuj: ^Ant.^ Voce mea ad Dóminum clamávi: neque obliviscétur miseréri Deus.
L.uwp: ^Ant.^ I have cried to the Lord with my voice, do not forget to show mercy, O God.
L.veo: ^Ant.^ Memor fuit in sǽculum * testaménti sui Dóminus Deus noster.
L.6y8: ^104:1^ Confitémini Dómino, et invocáte nomen eius: * annuntiáte inter gentes ópera eius.
L.6ys: ^104:2^ Cantáte ei, et psállite ei: * narráte ómnia mirabília eius.
L.6zf: ^104:3^ Laudámini in nómine sancto eius: * lætétur cor quæréntium Dóminum.
L.6zs: ^104:4^ Quǽrite Dóminum, et confirmámini: * quǽrite fáciem eius semper.
L.6zu: ^104:5^ Mementóte mirabílium eius, quæ fecit: * prodígia eius, et iudícia oris eius.
L.6zx: ^104:6^ Semen Ábraham, servi eius: * fílii Iacob, elécti eius.
L.6zz: ^104:7^ Ipse Dóminus Deus noster: * in univérsa terra iudícia eius.
L.701: ^104:8^ Memor fuit in sǽculum testaménti sui: * verbi, quod mandávit in mille generatiónes:
L.702: ^104:9^ Quod dispósuit ad Ábraham: * et iuraménti sui ad Isaac:
L.6xp: ^104:10^ Et státuit illud Iacob in præcéptum: * et Israël in testaméntum ætérnum:
L.6xq: ^104:11^ Dicens: Tibi dabo terram Chánaan, * funículum hereditátis vestræ.
L.6xs: ^104:12^ Cum essent número brevi, * paucíssimi et íncolæ eius:
L.6xv: ^104:13^ Et pertransiérunt de gente in gentem, * et de regno ad pópulum álterum.
L.6xx: ^104:14^ Non relíquit hóminem nocére eis: * et corrípuit pro eis reges.
L.6xy: ^104:15^ Nolíte tángere christos meos: * et in prophétis meis nolíte malignári.
L.vep: ^Ant.^ Memor fuit in sǽculum testaménti sui Dóminus Deus noster.
L.wig: ^Ant.^ The memory of thy testament * will live forever, O Lord our God.
L.6y9: ^104:1^ Give glory to the Lord, and call upon his name: * declare his deeds among the Gentiles.
L.6yt: ^104:2^ Sing to him, yea sing praises to him: * relate all his wondrous works.
L.6ze: ^104:3^ Glory ye in his holy name: * let the heart of them rejoice that seek the Lord.
L.6zt: ^104:4^ Seek ye the Lord, and be strengthened: * seek his face evermore.
L.6zv: ^104:5^ Remember his marvellous works which he hath done; * his wonders, and the judgments of his mouth.
L.6zw: ^104:6^ O ye seed of Abraham his servant; * ye sons of Jacob his chosen.
L.6zy: ^104:7^ He is the Lord our God: * his judgments are in all the earth.
L.700: ^104:8^ He hath remembered his covenant for ever: * the word which he commanded to a thousand generations.
L.703: ^104:9^ Which he made to Abraham; * and his oath to Isaac:
L.6xo: ^104:10^ And he appointed the same to Jacob for a law, * and to Israel for an everlasting testament:
L.6xr: ^104:11^ Saying: To thee will I give the land of Chanaan, * the lot of your inheritance.
L.6xt: ^104:12^ When they were but a small number: * yea very few, and sojourners therein:
L.6xu: ^104:13^ And they passed from nation to nation, * and from one kingdom to another people.
L.6xw: ^104:14^ He suffered no man to hurt them: * and he reproved kings for their sakes.
L.6xz: ^104:15^ Touch ye not my anointed: * and do no evil to my prophets.
L.wih: ^Ant.^ The memory of thy testament will live forever, O Lord our God.
L.tun: ^Ant.^ Auxit Dóminus * pópulum suum: et firmávit eum super inimícos eius.
L.6y1: ^104:16^ Et vocávit famem super terram: * et omne firmaméntum panis contrívit.
L.6y3: ^104:17^ Misit ante eos virum: * in servum venúmdatus est Ioseph.
L.6y4: ^104:18^ Humiliavérunt in compédibus pedes eius, ferrum pertránsiit ánimam eius * donec veníret verbum eius.
L.6y6: ^104:19^ Elóquium Dómini inflammávit eum: * misit rex, et solvit eum; princeps populórum, et dimísit eum.
L.6ya: ^104:21^ Constítuit eum dóminum domus suæ: * et príncipem omnis possessiónis suæ:
L.6yd: ^104:22^ Ut erudíret príncipes eius sicut semetípsum: * et senes eius prudéntiam docéret.
L.6yf: ^104:23^ Et intrávit Israël in Ægýptum: * et Iacob áccola fuit in terra Cham.
L.6yh: ^104:24^ Et auxit pópulum suum veheménter: * et firmávit eum super inimícos eius.
L.6yi: ^104:25^ Convértit cor eórum ut odírent pópulum eius: * et dolum fácerent in servos eius.
L.6yl: ^104:26^ Misit Móysen, servum suum: * Aaron, quem elégit ipsum.
L.6yn: ^104:27^ Pósuit in eis verba signórum suórum: * et prodigiórum in terra Cham.
L.tuo: ^Ant.^ Auxit Dóminus pópulum suum: et firmávit eum super inimícos eius.
L.wdd: ^Ant.^ The Lord increased his people exceedingly * and strengthened them over their enemies.
L.6y0: ^104:16^ And he called a famine upon the land: * and he broke in pieces all the support of bread.
L.6y2: ^104:17^ He sent a man before them: * Joseph, who was sold for a slave.
L.6y5: ^104:18^ They humbled his feet in fetters: the iron pierced his soul, * until his word came.
L.6y7: ^104:19^ The word of the Lord inflamed him: * the king sent, and he released him: the ruler of the people, and he set him at liberty.
L.6yb: ^104:21^ He made him master of his house, * and ruler of all his possession.
L.6yc: ^104:22^ That he might instruct his princes as himself, * and teach his ancients wisdom.
L.6ye: ^104:23^ And Israel went into Egypt: * and Jacob was a sojourner in the land of Cham.
L.6yg: ^104:24^ And he increased his people exceedingly: * and strengthened them over their enemies,
L.6yj: ^104:25^ He turned their heart to hate his people: * and to deal deceitfully with his servants.
L.6yk: ^104:26^ He sent Moses his servant: * Aaron the man whom he had chosen.
L.6ym: ^104:27^ He gave them power to shew his signs, * and his wonders in the land of Cham.
L.wde: ^Ant.^ The Lord increased his people exceedingly and strengthened them over their enemies.
L.uga: ^Ant.^ Edúxit Deus * pópulum suum in exsultatióne, et eléctos suos in lætítia.
L.6yp: ^104:28^ Misit ténebras, et obscurávit: * et non exacerbávit sermónes suos.
L.6yq: ^104:29^ Convértit aquas eórum in sánguinem: * et occídit pisces eórum.
L.6yv: ^104:30^ Édidit terra eórum ranas: * in penetrálibus regum ipsórum.
L.6yw: ^104:31^ Dixit, et venit cœnomyía: * et cínifes in ómnibus fínibus eórum.
L.6yz: ^104:32^ Pósuit plúvias eórum grándinem: * ignem comburéntem in terra ipsórum.
L.6z1: ^104:33^ Et percússit víneas eórum, et ficúlneas eórum: * et contrívit lignum fínium eórum.
L.6z2: ^104:34^ Dixit, et venit locústa, et bruchus, * cuius non erat númerus:
L.6z5: ^104:35^ Et comédit omne fænum in terra eórum: * et comédit omnem fructum terræ eórum.
L.6z7: ^104:36^ Et percússit omne primogénitum in terra eórum: * primítias omnis labóris eórum.
L.6z9: ^104:37^ Et edúxit eos cum argénto et auro: * et non erat in tríbubus eórum infírmus.
L.6zb: ^104:38^ Lætáta est Ægýptus in profectióne eórum: * quia incúbuit timor eórum super eos.
L.6zc: ^104:39^ Expándit nubem in protectiónem eórum: * et ignem ut lucéret eis per noctem.
L.6zg: ^104:40^ Petiérunt, et venit cotúrnix: * et pane cæli saturávit eos.
L.6zi: ^104:41^ Dirúpit petram et fluxérunt aquæ: * abiérunt in sicco flúmina;
L.6zl: ^104:42^ Quóniam memor fuit verbi sancti sui: * quod hábuit ad Ábraham, púerum suum.
L.6zn: ^104:43^ Et edúxit pópulum suum in exsultatióne, * et eléctos suos in lætítia.
L.6zp: ^104:44^ Et dedit illis regiónes géntium: * et labóres populórum possedérunt:
L.6zr: ^104:45^ Ut custódiant iustificatiónes eius, * et legem eius requírant.
L.ugb: ^Ant.^ Edúxit Deus pópulum suum in exsultatióne, et eléctos suos in lætítia.
L.wbz: ^Ant.^ The Lord brought forth * his people with joy, and his chosen with gladness.
L.6yo: ^104:28^ He sent darkness, and made it obscure: * and grieved not his words.
L.6yr: ^104:29^ He turned their waters into blood, * and destroyed their fish.
L.6yu: ^104:30^ Their land brought forth frogs, * in the inner chambers of their kings.
L.6yx: ^104:31^ He spoke, and there came diverse sorts of flies, * and sciniphs in all their coasts.
L.6yy: ^104:32^ He gave them hail for rain, * a burning fire in the land.
L.6z0: ^104:33^ And he destroyed their vineyards, and their fig trees: * and he broke in pieces the trees of their coasts.
L.6z3: ^104:34^ He spoke, and the locust came, and the bruchus, * of which there was no number.
L.6z4: ^104:35^ And they devoured all the grass in their land, * and consumed all the fruit of their ground.
L.6z6: ^104:36^ And he slew all the firstborn in their land: * the firstfruits of all their labour.
L.6z8: ^104:37^ And he brought them out with silver and gold: * and there was not among their tribes one that was feeble.
L.6za: ^104:38^ Egypt was glad when they departed: * for the fear of them lay upon them.
L.6zd: ^104:39^ He spread a cloud for their protection, * and fire to give them light in the night.
L.6zh: ^104:40^ They asked, and the quail came: * and he filled them with the bread of heaven.
L.6zj: ^104:41^ He opened the rock, and waters flowed: * rivers ran down in the dry land.
L.6zk: ^104:42^ Because he remembered his holy word, * which he had spoken to his servant Abraham.
L.6zm: ^104:43^ And he brought forth his people with joy, * and his chosen with gladness.
L.6zo: ^104:44^ And he gave them the lands of the Gentiles: * and they possessed the labours of the people:
L.6zq: ^104:45^ That they might observe his justifications, * and seek after his law.
L.wc0: ^Ant.^ The Lord brought forth his people with joy, and his chosen with gladness.
L.w2q: ^Ant.^ Salvávit eos Dóminus * propter nomen suum.
L.70o: ^105:1^ Confitémini Dómino, quóniam bonus: * quóniam in sǽculum misericórdia eius.
L.718: ^105:2^ Quis loquétur poténtias Dómini, * audítas fáciet omnes laudes eius?
L.71q: ^105:3^ Beáti, qui custódiunt iudícium, * et fáciunt iustítiam in omni témpore.
L.72c: ^105:4^ Meménto nostri, Dómine, in beneplácito pópuli tui: * vísita nos in salutári tuo:
L.72e: ^105:5^ Ad vidéndum in bonitáte electórum tuórum, ad lætándum in lætítia gentis tuæ: * ut laudéris cum hereditáte tua.
L.72g: ^105:6^ Peccávimus cum pátribus nostris: * iniúste égimus, iniquitátem fécimus.
L.72l: ^105:7^ Patres nostri in Ægýpto non intellexérunt mirabília tua: * non fuérunt mémores multitúdinis misericórdiæ tuæ.
L.72j: ^105:7^ Et irritavérunt ascendéntes in mare, * Mare Rubrum.
L.72n: ^105:8^ Et salvávit eos propter nomen suum: * ut notam fáceret poténtiam suam.
L.72p: ^105:9^ Et incrépuit Mare Rubrum, et exsiccátum est, * et dedúxit eos in abýssis sicut in desérto.
L.705: ^105:10^ Et salvávit eos de manu odiéntium: * et redémit eos de manu inimíci.
L.707: ^105:11^ Et opéruit aqua tribulántes eos: * unus ex eis non remánsit.
L.709: ^105:12^ Et credidérunt verbis eius: * et laudavérunt laudem eius.
L.70a: ^105:13^ Cito fecérunt, oblíti sunt óperum eius: * et non sustinuérunt consílium eius.
L.70d: ^105:14^ Et concupiérunt concupiscéntiam in desérto: * et tentavérunt Deum in inaquóso.
L.70f: ^105:15^ Et dedit eis petitiónem ipsórum: * et misit saturitátem in ánimas eórum.
L.w2r: ^Ant.^ Salvávit eos Dóminus propter nomen suum.
L.weg: ^Ant.^ The Lord saved them * for his own name's sake.
L.70p: ^105:1^ Give glory to the Lord, for he is good: * for his mercy endureth for ever.
L.719: ^105:2^ Who shall declare the powers of the Lord? * who shall set forth all his praises?
L.71r: ^105:3^ Blessed are they that keep judgment, * and do justice at all times.
L.72d: ^105:4^ Remember us, O Lord, in the favour of thy people: * visit us with thy salvation.
L.72f: ^105:5^ That we may see the good of thy chosen, that we may rejoice in the joy of thy nation: * that thou mayst be praised with thy inheritance.
L.72h: ^105:6^ We have sinned with our fathers: * we have acted unjustly, we have wrought iniquity.
L.72k: ^105:7^ Our fathers understood not thy wonders in Egypt: * they remembered not the multitude of thy mercies:
L.72i: ^105:7^ And they provoked to wrath going up to the sea, * even the Red Sea.
L.72m: ^105:8^ And he saved them for his own name’s sake: * that he might make his power known.
L.72o: ^105:9^ And he rebuked the Red Sea, and it was dried up: * and he led them through the depths, as in a wilderness.
L.704: ^105:10^ And he saved them from the hand of them that hated them: * and he redeemed them from the hand of the enemy.
L.706: ^105:11^ And the water covered them that afflicted them: * there was not one of them left.
L.708: ^105:12^ And they believed his words: * and they sang his praises.
L.70b: ^105:13^ They had quickly done, they forgot his works: * and they waited not for his counsels.
L.70c: ^105:14^ And they coveted their desire in the desert: * and they tempted God in the place without water.
L.70e: ^105:15^ And he gave them their request: * and sent fulness into their souls.
L.weh: ^Ant.^ The Lord saved them for his own name's sake.
L.vpq: ^Ant.^ Oblíti sunt Deum * qui salvávit eos.
L.70h: ^105:16^ Et irritavérunt Móysen in castris: * Aaron, sanctum Dómini.
L.70i: ^105:17^ Apérta est terra, et deglutívit Dathan: * et opéruit super congregatiónem Abíron.
L.70l: ^105:18^ Et exársit ignis in synagóga eórum * flamma combússit peccatóres.
L.70m: ^105:19^ Et fecérunt vítulum in Horeb * et adoravérunt scúlptile.
L.70r: ^105:20^ Et mutavérunt glóriam suam * in similitúdinem vítuli comedéntis fænum.
L.70s: ^105:21^ Oblíti sunt Deum, qui salvávit eos, * qui fecit magnália in Ægýpto, mirabília in terra Cham: terribília in Mari Rubro.
L.70v: ^105:23^ Et dixit ut dispérderet eos: * si non Móyses, eléctus eius, stetísset in confractióne in conspéctu eius:
L.70x: ^105:24^ Ut avérteret iram eius ne dispérderet eos: * et pro níhilo habuérunt terram desiderábilem:
L.70y: ^105:25^ Non credidérunt verbo eius, et murmuravérunt in tabernáculis suis: * non exaudiérunt vocem Dómini.
L.711: ^105:26^ Et elevávit manum suam super eos: * ut prostérneret eos in desérto:
L.713: ^105:27^ Et ut deíceret semen eórum in natiónibus: * et dispérgeret eos in regiónibus.
L.714: ^105:28^ Et initiáti sunt Beélphegor: * et comedérunt sacrifícia mortuórum.
L.717: ^105:29^ Et irritavérunt eum in adinventiónibus suis: * et multiplicáta est in eis ruína.
L.71a: ^105:30^ Et stetit Phínees, et placávit: * et cessávit quassátio.
L.71d: ^105:31^ Et reputátum est ei in iustítiam: * in generatiónem et generatiónem usque in sempitérnum.
L.vpr: ^Ant.^ Oblíti sunt Deum qui salvávit eos.
L.wl6: ^Ant.^ They forgot God * who saved them.
L.70g: ^105:16^ And they provoked Moses in the camp, * Aaron the holy one of the Lord.
L.70j: ^105:17^ The earth opened and swallowed up Dathan: * and covered the congregation of Abiron.
L.70k: ^105:18^ And a fire was kindled in their congregation: * the flame burned the wicked.
L.70n: ^105:19^ They made also a calf in Horeb: * and they adored the graven thing.
L.70q: ^105:20^ And they changed their glory * into the likeness of a calf that eateth grass.
L.70t: ^105:21^ They forgot God, who saved them, * who had done great things in Egypt, wondrous works in the land of Cham: terrible things in the Red Sea.
L.70u: ^105:23^ And he said that he would destroy them: * had not Moses his chosen stood before him in the breach:
L.70w: ^105:24^ To turn away his wrath, lest he should destroy them; * and they set at nought the desirable land.
L.70z: ^105:25^ They believed not his word, and they murmured in their tents: * they hearkened not to the voice of the Lord.
L.710: ^105:26^ And he lifted up his hand over them: * to overthrow them in the desert;
L.712: ^105:27^ And to cast down their seed among the nations, * and to scatter them in the countries.
L.715: ^105:28^ They also were initiated to Beelphegor: * and ate the sacrifices of the dead.
L.716: ^105:29^ And they provoked him with their inventions: * and destruction was multiplied among them.
L.71b: ^105:30^ Then Phinees stood up, and pacified him: * and the slaughter ceased.
L.71c: ^105:31^ And it was reputed to him unto justice, * to generation and generation for evermore.
L.wl7: ^Ant.^ They forgot God who saved them.
L.u7d: ^Ant.^ Cum tribularéntur * vidit Dóminus: et audívit oratiónem eórum.
L.71e: ^105:32^ Et irritavérunt eum ad aquas contradictiónis: * et vexátus est Móyses propter eos: quia exacerbavérunt spíritum eius.
L.71h: ^105:33^ Et distínxit in lábiis suis: * non disperdidérunt gentes, quas dixit Dóminus illis.
L.71j: ^105:35^ Et commísti sunt inter gentes, et didicérunt ópera eórum: et serviérunt sculptílibus eórum: * et factum est illis in scándalum.
L.71l: ^105:37^ Et immolavérunt fílios suos, * et fílias suas dæmóniis.
L.71n: ^105:38^ Et effudérunt sánguinem innocéntem: * sánguinem filiórum suórum et filiárum suárum, quas sacrificavérunt sculptílibus Chánaan.
L.71p: ^105:39^ Et infécta est terra in sanguínibus, et contamináta est in opéribus eórum: * et fornicáti sunt in adinventiónibus suis.
L.71t: ^105:40^ Et irátus est furóre Dóminus in pópulum suum: * et abominátus est hereditátem suam.
L.71v: ^105:41^ Et trádidit eos in manus géntium: * et domináti sunt eórum qui odérunt eos.
L.71x: ^105:42^ Et tribulavérunt eos inimíci eórum, et humiliáti sunt sub mánibus eórum: * sæpe liberávit eos.
L.71z: ^105:43^ Ipsi autem exacerbavérunt eum in consílio suo: * et humiliáti sunt in iniquitátibus suis.
L.721: ^105:44^ Et vidit, cum tribularéntur: * et audívit oratiónem eórum.
L.723: ^105:45^ Et memor fuit testaménti sui: * et pœnítuit eum secúndum multitúdinem misericórdiæ suæ.
L.725: ^105:46^ Et dedit eos in misericórdias * in conspéctu ómnium qui céperant eos.
L.726: ^105:47^ Salvos nos fac, Dómine, Deus noster: * et cóngrega nos de natiónibus:
L.729: ^105:47^ Ut confiteámur nómini sancto tuo: * et gloriémur in laude tua.
L.72a: ^105:48^ Benedíctus Dóminus, Deus Israël, a sǽculo et usque in sǽculum: * et dicet omnis pópulus: Fiat, fiat.
L.u7e: ^Ant.^ Cum tribularéntur vidit Dóminus: et audívit oratiónem eórum.
L.tpu: ^Ant.^ And he saw when they were in tribulation * and he heard their prayer.
L.71f: ^105:32^ They provoked him also at the waters of contradiction: * and Moses was afflicted for their sakes: because they exasperated his spirit.
L.71g: ^105:33^ And he distinguished with his lips; * they did not destroy the nations of which the Lord spoke unto them.
L.71i: ^105:35^ And they were mingled among the heathens, and learned their works: and served their idols, * and it became a stumblingblock to them.
L.71k: ^105:37^ And they sacrificed their sons, * and their daughters to devils.
L.71m: ^105:38^ And they shed innocent blood: * the blood of their sons and of their daughters which they sacrificed to the idols of Chanaan.
L.71o: ^105:39^ And the land was polluted with blood, and was defiled with their works: * and they went aside after their own inventions.
L.71s: ^105:40^ And the Lord was exceedingly angry with his people: * and he abhorred his inheritance.
L.71u: ^105:41^ And he delivered them into the hands of the nations: * and they that hated them had dominion over them.
L.71w: ^105:42^ And their enemies afflicted them: and they were humbled under their hands: * many times did he deliver them.
L.71y: ^105:43^ But they provoked him with their counsel: * and they were brought low by their iniquities.
L.720: ^105:44^ And he saw when they were in tribulation: * and he heard their prayer.
L.722: ^105:45^ And he was mindful of his covenant: * and repented according to the multitude of his mercies.
L.724: ^105:46^ And he gave them unto mercies, * in the sight of all those that had made them captives.
L.727: ^105:47^ Save us, O Lord, our God: * and gather us from among nations:
L.728: ^105:47^ That we may give thanks to thy holy name, * and may glory in thy praise.
L.72b: ^105:48^ Blessed be the Lord the God of Israel, from everlasting to everlasting: * and let all the people say: So be it, so be it.
L.tpv: ^Ant.^ And he saw when they were in tribulation and he heard their prayer.
L.u2z: ^Ant.^ Clamavérunt ad Dóminum * et de necessitátibus eórum liberávit eos.
L.73a: ^106:1^ Confitémini Dómino quóniam bonus: * quóniam in sǽculum misericórdia eius.
L.73w: ^106:2^ Dicant qui redémpti sunt a Dómino, quos redémit de manu inimíci: * et de regiónibus congregávit eos:
L.74i: ^106:3^ A solis ortu, et occásu: * ab aquilóne, et mari.
L.74s: ^106:4^ Erravérunt in solitúdine in inaquóso: * viam civitátis habitáculi non invenérunt.
L.74u: ^106:5^ Esuriéntes, et sitiéntes: * ánima eórum in ipsis defécit.
L.74x: ^106:6^ Et clamavérunt ad Dóminum cum tribularéntur: * et de necessitátibus eórum erípuit eos.
L.74z: ^106:7^ Et dedúxit eos in viam rectam: * ut irent in civitátem habitatiónis.
L.750: ^106:8^ Confiteántur Dómino misericórdiæ eius: * et mirabília eius fíliis hóminum.
L.753: ^106:9^ Quia satiávit ánimam inánem: * et ánimam esuriéntem satiávit bonis.
L.72q: ^106:10^ Sedéntes in ténebris, et umbra mortis: * vinctos in mendicitáte et ferro.
L.72t: ^106:11^ Quia exacerbavérunt elóquia Dei: * et consílium Altíssimi irritavérunt.
L.72v: ^106:12^ Et humiliátum est in labóribus cor eórum: * infirmáti sunt, nec fuit qui adiuváret.
L.72w: ^106:13^ Et clamavérunt ad Dóminum cum tribularéntur: * et de necessitátibus eórum liberávit eos.
L.72z: ^106:14^ Et edúxit eos de ténebris, et umbra mortis: * et víncula eórum disrúpit.
L.u30: ^Ant.^ Clamavérunt ad Dóminum et de necessitátibus eórum liberávit eos.
L.wk0: ^Ant.^ Then they cried to the Lord * and he delivered them out of their distresses.
L.73b: ^106:1^ Give glory to the Lord, for he is good: * for his mercy endureth for ever.
L.73x: ^106:2^ Let them say so that have been redeemed by the Lord, whom he hath redeemed from the hand of the enemy: * and gathered out of the countries.
L.74j: ^106:3^ From the rising and the setting of the sun, * from the north and from the sea.
L.74t: ^106:4^ They wandered in a wilderness, in a place without water: * they found not the way of a city for their habitation.
L.74v: ^106:5^ They were hungry and thirsty: * their soul fainted in them.
L.74w: ^106:6^ And they cried to the Lord in their tribulation: * and he delivered them out of their distresses.
L.74y: ^106:7^ And he led them into the right way: * that they might go to a city of habitation.
L.751: ^106:8^ Let the mercies of the Lord give glory to him: * and his wonderful works to the children of men.
L.752: ^106:9^ For he hath satisfied the empty soul, * and hath filled the hungry soul with good things.
L.72r: ^106:10^ Such as sat in darkness and in the shadow of death: * bound in want and in iron.
L.72s: ^106:11^ Because they had exasperated the words of God: * and provoked the counsel of the most High:
L.72u: ^106:12^ And their heart was humbled with labours: * they were weakened, and there was none to help them.
L.72x: ^106:13^ Then they cried to the Lord in their affliction: * and he delivered them out of their distresses.
L.72y: ^106:14^ And he brought them out of darkness, * and the shadow of death; and broke their bonds in sunder.
L.wk1: ^Ant.^ Then they cried to the Lord and he delivered them out of their distresses.
L.v4k: ^Ant.^ Ipsi vidérunt * ópera Dei et mirabília eius.
L.730: ^106:15^ Confiteántur Dómino misericórdiæ eius: * et mirabília eius fíliis hóminum.
L.733: ^106:16^ Quia contrívit portas ǽreas: * et vectes férreos confrégit.
L.735: ^106:17^ Suscépit eos de via iniquitátis eórum: * propter iniustítias enim suas humiliáti sunt.
L.736: ^106:18^ Omnem escam abomináta est ánima eórum: * et appropinquavérunt usque ad portas mortis.
L.739: ^106:19^ Et clamavérunt ad Dóminum cum tribularéntur: * et de necessitátibus eórum liberávit eos.
L.73d: ^106:20^ Misit verbum suum, et sanávit eos: * et erípuit eos de interitiónibus eórum.
L.73e: ^106:21^ Confiteántur Dómino misericórdiæ eius: * et mirabília eius fíliis hóminum.
L.73h: ^106:22^ Et sacríficent sacrifícium laudis: * et annúntient ópera eius in exsultatióne.
L.73i: ^106:23^ Qui descéndunt mare in návibus, * faciéntes operatiónem in aquis multis.
L.73k: ^106:24^ Ipsi vidérunt ópera Dómini, * et mirabília eius in profúndo.
L.73m: ^106:25^ Dixit, et stetit spíritus procéllæ: * et exaltáti sunt fluctus eius.
L.73o: ^106:26^ Ascéndunt usque ad cælos, et descéndunt usque ad abýssos: * ánima eórum in malis tabescébat.
L.73r: ^106:27^ Turbáti sunt, et moti sunt sicut ébrius: * et omnis sapiéntia eórum devoráta est.
L.73t: ^106:28^ Et clamavérunt ad Dóminum cum tribularéntur: * et de necessitátibus eórum edúxit eos.
L.73v: ^106:29^ Et státuit procéllam eius in auram: * et siluérunt fluctus eius.
L.73z: ^106:30^ Et lætáti sunt quia siluérunt: * et dedúxit eos in portum voluntátis eórum.
L.v4l: ^Ant.^ Ipsi vidérunt ópera Dei et mirabília eius.
L.wky: ^Ant.^ These have seen * the works of the Lord, and his wonders.
L.731: ^106:15^ Let the mercies of the Lord give glory to him, * and his wonderful works to the children of men.
L.732: ^106:16^ Because he hath broken gates of brass, * and burst the iron bars.
L.734: ^106:17^ He took them out of the way of their iniquity: * for they were brought low for their injustices.
L.737: ^106:18^ Their soul abhorred all manner of meat: * and they drew nigh even to the gates of death.
L.738: ^106:19^ And they cried to the Lord in their affliction: * and he delivered them out of their distresses.
L.73c: ^106:20^ He sent his word, and healed them: * and delivered them from their destructions.
L.73f: ^106:21^ Let the mercies of the Lord give glory to him: * and his wonderful works to the children of men.
L.73g: ^106:22^ And let them sacrifice the sacrifice of praise: * and declare his works with joy.
L.73j: ^106:23^ They that go down to the sea in ships, * doing business in the great waters:
L.73l: ^106:24^ These have seen the works of the Lord, * and his wonders in the deep.
L.73n: ^106:25^ He said the word, and there arose a storm of wind: * and the waves thereof were lifted up.
L.73p: ^106:26^ They mount up to the heavens, and they go down to the depths: * their soul pined away with evils.
L.73q: ^106:27^ They were troubled, and reeled like a drunken man; * and all their wisdom was swallowed up.
L.73s: ^106:28^ And they cried to the Lord in their affliction: * and he brought them out of their distresses.
L.73u: ^106:29^ And he turned the storm into a breeze: * and its waves were still.
L.73y: ^106:30^ And they rejoiced because they were still: * and he brought them to the haven which they wished for.
L.wkz: ^Ant.^ These have seen the works of the Lord, and his wonders.
L.wth: ^Ant.^ Vidébunt recti * et lætabúntur, et intéllegent misericórdias Dómini.
L.740: ^106:31^ Confiteántur Dómino misericórdiæ eius: * et mirabília eius fíliis hóminum.
L.743: ^106:32^ Et exáltent eum in ecclésia plebis: * et in cáthedra seniórum laudent eum.
L.745: ^106:33^ Pósuit flúmina in desértum: * et éxitus aquárum in sitim.
L.747: ^106:34^ Terram fructíferam in salsúginem: * a malítia inhabitántium in ea.
L.749: ^106:35^ Pósuit desértum in stagna aquárum: * et terram sine aqua in éxitus aquárum.
L.74b: ^106:36^ Et collocávit illic esuriéntes: * et constituérunt civitátem habitatiónis.
L.74d: ^106:37^ Et seminavérunt agros, et plantavérunt víneas: * et fecérunt fructum nativitátis.
L.74f: ^106:38^ Et benedíxit eis, et multiplicáti sunt nimis: * et iuménta eórum non minorávit.
L.74g: ^106:39^ Et pauci facti sunt: * et vexáti sunt a tribulatióne malórum, et dolóre.
L.74l: ^106:40^ Effúsa est contémptio super príncipes: * et erráre fecit eos in ínvio, et non in via.
L.74n: ^106:41^ Et adiúvit páuperem de inópia: * et pósuit sicut oves famílias.
L.74p: ^106:42^ Vidébunt recti, et lætabúntur: * et omnis iníquitas oppilábit os suum.
L.74q: ^106:43^ Quis sápiens et custódiet hæc? * et intélleget misericórdias Dómini.
L.wti: ^Ant.^ Vidébunt recti et lætabúntur, et intéllegent misericórdias Dómini.
L.why: ^Ant.^ The just see and rejoice * and understand the mercy of the Lord.
L.741: ^106:31^ Let the mercies of the Lord give glory to him, * and his wonderful works to the children of men.
L.742: ^106:32^ And let them exalt him in the church of the people: * and praise him in the chair of the ancients.
L.744: ^106:33^ He hath turned rivers into a wilderness: * and the sources of water into dry ground:
L.746: ^106:34^ A fruitful land into barrenness, * for the wickedness of them that dwell therein.
L.748: ^106:35^ He hath turned a wilderness into pools of water, * and a dry land into water springs.
L.74a: ^106:36^ And hath placed there the hungry; * and they made a city for their habitation.
L.74c: ^106:37^ And they sowed fields, and planted vineyards: * and they yielded fruit of birth.
L.74e: ^106:38^ And he blessed them, and they were multiplied exceedingly: * and their cattle he suffered not to decrease.
L.74h: ^106:39^ Then they were brought to be few: * and they were afflicted through the trouble of evils and sorrow.
L.74k: ^106:40^ Contempt was poured forth upon their princes: * and he caused them to wander where there was no passing, and out of the way.
L.74m: ^106:41^ And he helped the poor out of poverty: * and made him families like a flock of sheep.
L.74o: ^106:42^ The just shall see, and shall rejoice, * and all iniquity shall stop their mouth.
L.74r: ^106:43^ Who is wise, and will keep these things: * and will understand the mercies of the Lord?
L.whz: ^Ant.^ The just see and rejoice and understand the mercy of the Lord.
L.fvg: ^℟.^ Et in cáthedra seniórum laudent eum.
L.110p: ^℣.^ Let them exalt the Lord in the church of the people.
L.z04: ^℟.^ And praise him in the chair of the ancients.

L.vwl: ^Ant.^ Quam magnificáta sunt ópera tua, Dómine.
L.vlv: ^Ant.^ O Lord, * how great are thy works!
L.vmh: ^Ant.^ O Lord, how great are thy works!
L.vbt: ^Ant.^ Lætábitur iustus * in Dómino et sperábit in eo.
L.vbu: ^Ant.^ Lætábitur iustus in Dómino et sperábit in eo.
L.wi0: ^Ant.^ The just shall rejoice * in the Lord, and shall hope in him.
L.wi1: ^Ant.^ The just shall rejoice in the Lord, and shall hope in him.
L.vrm: ^Ant.^ Osténde nobis, Dómine, * lucem miseratiónum tuárum.
L.7jv: ^36:1^ Miserére nostri, Deus ómnium, et réspice nos, * et osténde nobis lucem miseratiónum tuárum:
L.7kk: ^36:2^ Et immítte timórem tuum super gentes, * quæ non exquisiérunt te,
L.7la: ^36:3^ Ut cognóscant quia non est Deus nisi tu, * et enárrent magnália tua.
L.7lg: ^36:4^ Álleva manum tuam super gentes aliénas, * ut vídeant poténtiam tuam.
L.7lk: ^36:5^ Sicut enim in conspéctu eórum sanctificátus es in nobis, * sic in conspéctu nostro magnificáberis in eis,
L.7lo: ^36:6^ Ut cognóscant te, sicut et nos cognóvimus, * quóniam non est Deus præter te, Dómine.
L.7ls: ^36:7^ Ínnova signa, et immúta mirabília. * Glorífica manum, et brácchium dextrum.
L.7lw: ^36:8^ Éxcita furórem, et effúnde iram. * Tolle adversárium, et afflíge inimícum.
L.7lx: ^36:9^ Festína tempus, et meménto finis, * ut enárrent mirabília tua.
L.7iv: ^36:10^ In ira flammæ devorétur qui salvátur: * et qui péssimant plebem tuam, invéniant perditiónem.
L.7iz: ^36:11^ Cóntere caput príncipum inimicórum, * dicéntium: Non est álius præter nos.
L.7j1: ^36:12^ Cóngrega omnes tribus Iacob: ut cognóscant quia non est Deus nisi tu, * et enárrent magnália tua:
L.7j8: ^36:13^ Et hereditábis eos, * sicut ab inítio.
L.7jb: ^36:14^ Miserére plebi tuæ, super quam invocátum est nomen tuum: * et Israël, quem coæquásti primogénito tuo.
L.7ji: ^36:15^ Miserére civitáti sanctificatiónis tuæ Ierúsalem, * civitáti requiéi tuæ.
L.7jm: ^36:16^ Reple Sion inenarrabílibus verbis tuis, * et glória tua pópulum tuum.
L.vrn: ^Ant.^ Osténde nobis, Dómine, lucem miseratiónum tuárum.
L.w5b: ^Ant.^ Show us, O Lord, * the light of thy mercies.
L.7ju: ^36:1^ Have mercy upon us, O God of all, and behold us, * and shew us the light of thy mercies:
L.7kj: ^36:2^ And send thy fear upon the nations, * that have not sought after thee:
L.7l8: ^36:3^ That they may know that there is no God beside thee, * and that they may shew forth thy wonders.
L.7lf: ^36:4^ Lift up thy hand over the strange nations, * that they may see thy power.
L.7li: ^36:5^ For as thou hast been sanctified in us in their sight, * so thou shalt be magnified among them in our presence,
L.7ln: ^36:6^ That they may know thee, as we also have known thee, * that there is no God beside thee, O Lord.
L.7lr: ^36:7^ Renew thy signs, and work new miracles. * Glorify thy hand, and thy right arm.
L.7lv: ^36:8^ Raise up indignation, and pour out wrath. * Take away the adversary, and crush the enemy.
L.7lz: ^36:9^ Hasten the time, and remember the end, * that they may declare thy wonderful works.
L.7iw: ^36:10^ Let him that escapeth be consumed by the rage of the fire: * and let them perish that oppress thy people.
L.7iy: ^36:11^ Crush the head of the princes of the enemies * that say: There is no other beside us.
L.7j2: ^36:12^ Gather together all the tribes of Jacob: that they may know that there is no God besides thee, * and may declare thy great works.
L.7j5: ^36:13^ And thou shalt inherit them * as from the beginning.
L.7ja: ^36:14^ Have mercy on thy people, upon whom thy name is invoked: * and upon Israel, whom thou hast raised up to be thy firstborn.
L.7jg: ^36:15^ Have mercy on Jerusalem, the city which thou hast sanctified, * the city of thy rest.
L.7jk: ^36:16^ Fill Sion with thy unspeakable words, * and thy people with thy glory.
L.w5c: ^Ant.^ Show us, O Lord, the light of thy mercies.
L.v90: ^Ant.^ Let every thing that hath breath * praise the Lord.
L.v91: ^Ant.^ Let every thing that hath breath praise the Lord.
L.ujq: ^Ant.^ Exaltáre, Dómine, * qui iúdicas terram: redde retributiónem supérbis.
L.va6: ^Ant.^ Lift up thyself, O Lord, * thou that judgest the earth: render retribution to the proud.
L.krm: In illo témpore: Loquénte Iesu ad turbas, extóllens vocem quædam múlier de turba, dixit illi: Beátus venter, qui te portávit, et úbera, quæ suxísti.
L.inf: At that time, as Jesus was speaking to the multitudes, a certain woman from the crowd lifted up her voice and said to Him, Blessed is the womb that bore You, and the breasts that nursed You. But He said, Rather, blessed are they who hear the word of God and keep it.
L.u31: ^Ant.^ Clamor meus, * Dómine, ad te pervéniat: non avértas fáciem tuam a me.
L.v94: ^Ant.^ Let my cry reach unto thee, O Lord: * turn not away thy face from me.
L.c1f: ^101:14^ Tu exsúrgens miseréberis Sion: * quia tempus miseréndi eius, quia venit tempus.
L.c1h: ^101:15^ Quóniam placuérunt servis tuis lápides eius: * et terræ eius miserebúntur.
L.c1j: ^101:16^ Et timébunt gentes nomen tuum, Dómine, * et omnes reges terræ glóriam tuam.
L.c1l: ^101:17^ Quia ædificávit Dóminus Sion: * et vidébitur in glória sua.
L.c1n: ^101:18^ Respéxit in oratiónem humílium: * et non sprevit precem eórum.
L.c1p: ^101:19^ Scribántur hæc in generatióne áltera: * et pópulus, qui creábitur, laudábit Dóminum:
L.c1r: ^101:20^ Quia prospéxit de excélso sancto suo: * Dóminus de cælo in terram aspéxit:
L.c1t: ^101:21^ Ut audíret gémitus compeditórum: * ut sólveret fílios interemptórum:

Thus in the chosen city He has given me rest, in Jerusalem is my domain. I have struck root among the glorious people, in the portion of my God, His heritage, and my abode is in the full assembly of Saints.

L.ka6: Hail, Mary, full of grace, the Lord is with you. Blessed are you among women and blessed is the fruit of your womb.
L.odv: Vere dignum et iustum est, æquum et salutáre, nos tibi semper et ubíque grátias ágere: Dómine sancte, Pater omnípotens, ætérne Deus: Et te in veneratione beátæ Maríæ semper Vírginis collaudáre, benedícere et prædicáre. Quæ et Unigénitum tuum Sancti Spíritus obumbratióne concépit: et, virginitátis glória permanénte, lumen ætérnum mundo effúdit, Iesum Christum, Dóminum nostrum. Per quem maiestátem tuam laudant Angeli, adórant Dominatiónes, tremunt Potestátes. Cæli cælorúmque Virtútes ac beáta Séraphim sócia exsultatióne concélebrant. Cum quibus et nostras voces ut admítti iubeas, deprecámur, súpplici confessióne dicéntes:
L.l0n: It is truly meet and just, right and for our salvation, that we should at all times, and in all places, give thanks unto Thee, O holy Lord, Father almighty, everlasting God: and that we should praise and bless, and proclaim Thee, in the veneration of the Blessed Mary, ever-Virgin: Who also conceived Thine only-begotten Son by the overshadowing of the Holy Ghost, and the glory of her virginity still abiding, gave forth to the world the everlasting Light, Jesus Christ our Lord. Through whom the Angels praise Thy Majesty, the Dominations worship it, and the Powers stand in awe. The Heavens and the heavenly hosts together with the blessed Seraphim in triumphant chorus unite to celebrate it. Together with these we entreat Thee that Thou mayest bid our voices also to be admitted while we say with lowly praise:
